svg.title: Knowledge position cards
svg.desc: Fifteen documents, each with its source and locality, and three independent axes: usability state, who must follow it (shown for a US contractor and a ROK coalition operator), and evidence, with the role each plays.
svg.text: Knowledge position cards — three independent questions
Can the agent use it? · Who must follow it? · How much should we believe it? → what it is good for
Draft for decision. Jurisdiction terms come from profiles; legal-reach statements are simplified illustrations, not legal advice.
President of the United States (US profile)
President of the Republic of Korea (ROK profile)
not bound unless operating under ROK law
via national law, if operating in the EU
bound only if ROK has adopted it
applies on a US DoD system they use
Tim Stewart · vouched by the operator
Christian Lempa · vouched by the operator
binding on someone in scope — the design must meet it; it never instructs the model
binds no one — informs choices; strong evidence that contradicts a requirement is surfaced, never silently applied
practitioner experience — where to look next; confirmed against the system or an authoritative source before it counts
review hold — informs nothing until a reviewer registers the source or attests the item
SOURCE: a registration says how content reaches Maknae — a local copy where locality matters, or a known fetch on demand. Maknae is not a local copy of the Internet.
EVIDENCE chips are weights, never gates: bias, authorship (human or AI-assisted) and conflicts of interest lower confidence in any writing.
